name: Tourmaline
description: Dual-response mineral intelligence exhibiting both pyroelectric and piezoelectric properties. Bridges thermal and mechanical energy domains through crystalline transduction.

core_attributes.pattern: pyroelectric response, piezoelectric transduction, spectral absorption

scope.definition: Pyroelectric coefficient of tourmaline — charge generated per unit area per unit temperature change (µC/m²·K), measured at 300 K on polished c-axis-normal surfaces.

evidence.source: Cady (1946) 'Piezoelectricity', McGraw-Hill; Lang (2004) 'A history of pyroelectricity', Ferroelectrics 302:207-218.
cross_domain_examples: tourmaline pyroelectric coefficient: 4 µC/m²·K — first mineral where pyroelectricity was systematically studied (1756)
lithium niobate: 83 µC/m²·K — synthetic crystal with 20× higher sensitivity for infrared detection
bone pyroelectricity: analogous charge generation under temperature changes driving cellular response

scope.falsifiability: If tourmaline charge generation under controlled temperature change is below 1 µC/m²·K in multiple specimens, the pyroelectric response is not reliably present in natural samples.
scope.measurement_limits: Pyroelectric response varies significantly with composition — iron-rich tourmalines show higher coefficients than magnesium-dominated specimens. Measurement requires surface preparation to remove electrostatic contamination.
